question: Explain the main electrostatic properties of a charged conductor in equilibrium. Hence find the electric potential at the surface and at the centre of an isolated conducting sphere of radius $10\text{ cm}$ carrying charge $5.0\ \mu\text{C}$.

options.A: In equilibrium, electric field inside is nonzero, charge is uniformly distributed throughout volume, and the conductor is not equipotential. Both surface and centre potential are $4.5\times10^4\text{ V}$.
options.B: In electrostatic equilibrium, $E=0$ inside the conductor, excess charge resides on the outer surface, and the electric field just outside is normal to the surface. The conductor is equipotential. Hence $V_{\text{surface}}=V_{\text{centre}}=\dfrac{kQ}{R}=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times5.0\times10^{-6}}{0.10}=4.5\times10^5\text{ V}$.
options.C: A charged conductor is equipotential only on its surface, not inside. Thus $V_{\text{surface}}=4.5\times10^5\text{ V}$ and $V_{\text{centre}}=0$.
options.D: Charge stays inside the conductor in equilibrium, and the potential at the centre is $9.0\times10^5\text{ V}$.
